items.title: Regular matrix polynomials and homogeneous eigenpairs
items.statement:
Fix integers $n,m\ge1$ and coefficient matrices $A_0,\ldots,A_m\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}$. The **grade-$m$ matrix polynomial** is
$$P(\lambda):=\sum_{j=0}^{m}A_j\lambda^j.$$
When $P$ is not identically zero, its actual degree is the degree of its largest nonzero scalar entry and can be smaller than the declared grade $m$; the zero polynomial has no actual degree. It is **regular** when the scalar polynomial $\det P(\lambda)$ is not identically zero. Write $x^*$ for conjugate transpose, $\langle u,v\rangle:=v^*u$ for the Euclidean inner product, $\|x\|_2:=(x^*x)^{1/2}$ for the Euclidean vector norm, and $\|M\|_F:=(\sum_{r,s}|M_{rs}|^2)^{1/2}$ for the Frobenius matrix norm.

The **grade-$m$ homogeneous polynomial** is
$$P_h(\alpha,\beta):=\sum_{j=0}^{m}A_j\alpha^j\beta^{m-j}.$$
A projective parameter $[\alpha:\beta]$ is a nonzero pair $(\alpha,\beta)\in\mathbb C^2$ modulo common multiplication by a nonzero scalar. A **homogeneous eigenpair** is $([\alpha:\beta],x)$ with $x\in\mathbb C^n\setminus\{0\}$ and $P_h(\alpha,\beta)x=0$. This condition is independent of the representative because $P_h(c\alpha,c\beta)=c^mP_h(\alpha,\beta)$. If $\beta\ne0$, the associated finite parameter is $\lambda=\alpha/\beta$ and $P_h(\alpha,\beta)=\beta^mP(\lambda)$. The point $[1:0]$ is the parameter at infinity; there $P_h(1,0)=A_m$, so it is an eigenvalue exactly when $A_m$ is singular. For regular $P$, the algebraic multiplicity at a finite $\lambda_0$ is the order of the zero of $\det P$ at $\lambda_0$. The **reversal** is $P^{\rm rev}_m(\mu):=\sum_{j=0}^{m}A_{m-j}\mu^j=\mu^mP(1/\mu)$; the algebraic multiplicity at infinity is the order of the zero of $\det P^{\rm rev}_m$ at $\mu=0$. The order of a zero at $0$ is the largest integer $r$ for which $\mu^r$ divides the scalar polynomial.

items.title: First Frobenius companion pencil of a matrix polynomial
items.statement:
Let $P(\lambda)=\sum_{j=0}^{m}A_j\lambda^j$ be as in [[def-matrix-polynomial-and-homogeneous-eigenpairs]]. For $m\ge1$, define $mn\times mn$ block matrices $A_c,B_c$ by
$$A_c:=\begin{bmatrix}A_{m-1}&A_{m-2}&\cdots&A_0\\-I_n&0&\cdots&0\\0&-I_n&\ddots&\vdots\\\vdots&\ddots&\ddots&0\\0&\cdots&-I_n&0\end{bmatrix},\qquad B_c:=\begin{bmatrix}-A_m&0&\cdots&0\\0&-I_n&\cdots&0\\\vdots&\ddots&\ddots&\vdots\\0&\cdots&0&-I_n\end{bmatrix}.$$
The **first Frobenius companion pencil** with the sign convention used here is
$$L(\lambda):=A_c-\lambda B_c=\begin{bmatrix}\lambda A_m+A_{m-1}&A_{m-2}&\cdots&A_0\\-I_n&\lambda I_n&\cdots&0\\0&-I_n&\ddots&\vdots\\\vdots&\ddots&\ddots&\lambda I_n\end{bmatrix}.$$
For a vector $x\in\mathbb C^n$ and finite $\lambda$, its **companion lift** is $z(\lambda,x):=(\lambda^{m-1}x,\lambda^{m-2}x,\ldots,\lambda x,x)^T\in\mathbb C^{mn}$; when $m=1$, this is simply $x$.

items.title: The first Frobenius companion pencil preserves the finite and infinite polynomial spectrum
items.statement: Let $P$ be a regular $n\times n$ grade-$m$ matrix polynomial with $m\ge1$, and let $L(\lambda)=A_c-\lambda B_c$ be the pencil of [[def-first-frobenius-companion-pencil]]. A square matrix polynomial is **unimodular** when its determinant is a nonzero constant. The pencil $L$ is a **strong linearization** of $P$ if there are unimodular polynomial matrices $U,V$ with $ULV=\operatorname{diag}(P,I_{(m-1)n})$ and unimodular polynomial matrices $\widetilde U,\widetilde V$ with $\widetilde U(\mu)(\mu A_c-B_c)\widetilde V(\mu)=\operatorname{diag}(P^{\rm rev}_m,I_{(m-1)n})$. Such matrices exist. In particular, $\det(A_c-\lambda B_c)=\det P(\lambda)$; finite eigenvectors correspond by $x\mapsto z(\lambda,x)$; and the infinite eigenspaces correspond by $x\mapsto(x,0,\ldots,0)^T$ from $\ker A_m$ to $\ker(-B_c)$. The algebraic multiplicity of infinity in both problems is $mn-\deg\det P$. Thus if $A_m$ is invertible there are no infinite eigenvalues; if $A_m$ is singular there is at least one, with geometric multiplicity $\dim\ker A_m$, which need not equal its algebraic multiplicity.

items.title: A companion-pencil residual transfers to the polynomial residual through explicit block factors
items.statement:
Let $P(\lambda)=\sum_{j=0}^{m}A_j\lambda^j$ have grade $m\ge1$, and let $L(\lambda)$ be its first companion pencil. For any block vector $z=(z_1,\ldots,z_m)^T$, write its pencil residual as $e=L(\lambda)z=(e_1,\ldots,e_m)^T$ and put $x=z_m$. For $2\le k\le m$, set
$$Q_k(\lambda):=\sum_{j=m-k+1}^{m}A_j\lambda^{j-m+k-1}.$$
Then the exact identity and norm bound are
$$P(\lambda)x=e_1+\sum_{k=2}^{m}Q_k(\lambda)e_k,\qquad \|P(\lambda)x\|_2\le\|e_1\|_2+\sum_{k=2}^{m}\|Q_k(\lambda)\|_F\|e_k\|_2.$$
Empty sums are zero when $m=1$. In particular, the companion lift has $e_2=\cdots=e_m=0$ and $e_1=P(\lambda)x$. The displayed factors depend on $\lambda$ and the coefficients, so an unscaled pencil residual by itself supplies no uniform polynomial-residual bound and no polynomial conditioning claim.

items.title: Coefficientwise weighted Frobenius backward error for a polynomial eigenpair
items.statement:
Let $P(\lambda)=\sum_{j=0}^{m}A_j\lambda^j$ be regular of grade $m$, let $[\alpha:\beta]$ be a projective parameter, let $x\in\mathbb C^n\setminus\{0\}$, and choose positive weights $\omega_0,\ldots,\omega_m$. Write $r:=P_h(\alpha,\beta)x$. The **coefficientwise weighted Frobenius backward error** is the infimum
$$\eta_F(P,[\alpha:\beta],x;\omega):=\inf\left\{\left(\sum_{j=0}^{m}\frac{\|\Delta A_j\|_F^2}{\omega_j^2}\right)^{1/2}:\ \sum_{j=0}^{m}(A_j+\Delta A_j)\alpha^j\beta^{m-j}x=0,\quad \Delta A_j\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}\right\}.$$
The perturbations of distinct coefficients are unrestricted and measured in the displayed weighted product norm; no symmetry or other coefficient structure is imposed. Replacing $(\alpha,\beta)$ by $(c\alpha,c\beta)$ for $c\ne0$ multiplies the constraint by $c^m$ and leaves its zero set unchanged, so the infimum depends only on $[\alpha:\beta]$. The infimum is defined for finite and infinite projective parameters. The next theorem proves that it is attained and gives its exact value.

items.title: Exact minimum formula for a fixed polynomial eigenpair's weighted backward error
items.statement:
Under the hypotheses of [[def-coefficientwise-weighted-backward-error-for-matrix-polynomial]], put
$$S:=\sum_{j=0}^{m}\omega_j^2|\alpha|^{2j}|\beta|^{2(m-j)}.$$
Then $S>0$, the infimum is attained, and
$$\eta_F(P,[\alpha:\beta],x;\omega)=\frac{\|P_h(\alpha,\beta)x\|_2}{\|x\|_2\sqrt{S}}.$$
At a finite parameter $[\lambda:1]$ this is $\|P(\lambda)x\|_2/(\|x\|_2\sqrt{\sum_j\omega_j^2|\lambda|^{2j}})$; at infinity $[1:0]$ it is $\|A_mx\|_2/(\omega_m\|x\|_2)$. When $\alpha\ne0$, setting $\mu=\beta/\alpha$ rewrites the same formula for $P^{\rm rev}_m(\mu)$ with reversed coefficient weights $\widetilde\omega_k:=\omega_{m-k}$.

items.title: Rational matrix eigenproblem on its pole-free domain
items.statement: Let $\mathbb C(\lambda)$ denote the field of quotients of complex scalar polynomials. Let $R(\lambda)\in\mathbb C(\lambda)^{n\times n}$ with $n\ge1$ be a square matrix whose entries are rational functions of $\lambda$. Write each entry as a reduced scalar fraction (common polynomial factors have been cancelled), and let $q(\lambda)$ be the monic least common multiple of their denominators. Thus the zero set $\mathcal P:=\{\lambda:q(\lambda)=0\}$ is exactly the set of poles of at least one entry. Define the pole-free domain $\Omega:=\mathbb C\setminus\mathcal P$ and the polynomial matrix $N(\lambda):=q(\lambda)R(\lambda)$, whose entries are polynomials as in [[def-matrix-polynomial-and-homogeneous-eigenpairs]]. A **rational eigenpair** is a pair $(\lambda,x)$ with $\lambda\in\Omega$, $x\in\mathbb C^n\setminus\{0\}$, and $R(\lambda)x=0$; its $\lambda$ is a rational eigenvalue. The **cleared-denominator polynomial equation** is $N(\lambda)x=0$, but it represents the rational eigenproblem only on $\Omega$. Any solution at a pole is an inadmissible candidate, even when the cleared polynomial matrix is singular there.

items.title: Clearing a common denominator preserves rational eigenpairs only away from poles
items.statement: Let $R=q^{-1}N$ and $\Omega$ be as in [[def-rational-matrix-eigenproblem-and-pole-domain]]. For every $\lambda\in\Omega$ and every nonzero $x$, $R(\lambda)x=0$ if and only if $N(\lambda)x=0$. No point of $\mathcal P=\mathbb C\setminus\Omega$ is a rational eigenvalue, regardless of whether $N(\lambda)$ is singular there.

items.title: A damped oscillator and its first companion pencil
items.statement:
Consider the scalar damped oscillator with mass $M=1$, damping coefficient $C=1/2$, and stiffness $K=2$. Its quadratic polynomial is $P(\lambda)=\lambda^2+(1/2)\lambda+2$. The first companion pencil is
$$L(\lambda)=\begin{bmatrix}\lambda+1/2&2\\-1&\lambda\end{bmatrix}.$$
This example checks its finite roots and the companion eigenvector lift.

items.title: A singular leading coefficient gives an infinite polynomial eigenvalue
items.statement: Take the grade-two matrix polynomial $P(\lambda)=\operatorname{diag}(1,\lambda^2)$, so $n=m=2$, $\det P(\lambda)=\lambda^2$, and $A_2=\operatorname{diag}(0,1)$ is singular. The finite root $\lambda=0$ and the infinite root are different projective eigenvalues. Their algebraic and geometric multiplicities are computed directly below.

items.title: A transfer-function pole becomes a spurious root after denominator clearing
items.statement:
The rational transfer matrix
$$R(\lambda)=\begin{bmatrix}(\lambda-1)^{-1}&0\\0&1\end{bmatrix}$$
has a pole at $\lambda=1$. Here a finite-dimensional state-space transfer matrix means a rational matrix of the form $C(\lambda I-A)^{-1}B+D$; the displayed $R$ has such a realization with $A=[1]$, $B=[1\ 0]$, $C=[1\ 0]^T$, and $D=\operatorname{diag}(0,1)$. It has no rational eigenpair on its domain, but clearing the common denominator yields a polynomial matrix singular at the excluded pole.
